reference_sql:
SELECT MAX(t.n_lines) AS max_lines
FROM (
  -- one row per order
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
) AS t
alternatives:
WITH order_line_counts AS (
  -- one row per order
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT MAX(n_lines) AS max_lines
FROM order_line_counts

SELECT MAX(lines_per_order.n_lines) AS max_lines
FROM (
  -- one row per order
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(order_line_id) AS n_lines
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
) AS lines_per_order

other_way.sql:
WITH order_line_counts AS (
  -- one row per order
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT MAX(n_lines) AS max_lines
FROM order_line_counts
other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step gives the per-order counts a name before MAX reads them; for one short step the derived table is just as clear.
